Definition: an exploit (of God), or a performance (of man, often in a bad sense); by implication, an opportunity
BiblicalUsage: The doings of God, His exploits, and the Bible calls for them to be told. O give thanks unto the LORD; call upon his name: make known his deeds among the people. Isaiah says the same on the day of salvation: praise the LORD, declare His doings among the people, make mention that His name is exalted; the word is what God has done, and the command is to say it out loud.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for God's doings carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the command with it, that what God has done is not to be kept quiet but declared among the peoples.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
